P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No general exchange controls: there are no general restrictions on remittances to or from abroad, but sanctions and embargoes (OFAC) restrict payments involving listed countries and entities (Deloitte 2026). Reporting applies: US persons with foreign financial accounts whose combined value exceeds USD 10,000 at any time in the year must file an FBAR (IRS); banks file reports on cash transactions above USD 10,000 (not captured).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Legal, but rare for ordinary consumers. Large US retail banks such as Bank of America design personal accounts to hold USD only and do not offer personal foreign-currency accounts; foreign-currency options exist mainly for business and treasury clients (Exiap). Residents who need EUR or GBP balances usually use fintech multi-currency accounts (see P5) or a premium bank product.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Someone who owns an unincorporated business alone is a sole proprietor, with no federal registration needed beyond tax filing. They report on Form 1040 with Schedule C (profit or loss), Schedule SE (self-employment tax) and quarterly Form 1040-ES estimated tax. State/local business licences, DBA filings and sales-tax permits vary (not captured). A single-member LLC electing corporate treatment is not a sole proprietorship.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: The US taxes citizens and residents (green-card holders or substantial-presence test) on worldwide income. Federal rates run from 10% to 37% (2025 brackets; TCJA rates made permanent by the OBBBA). Self-employed people also pay 15.3% self-employment tax (12.4% Social Security up to the wage base plus 2.9% Medicare). State and local income taxes apply in most states.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: There is no federal VAT or sales tax. 45 states and DC impose sales and use taxes (state rates about 2.9%-7.25%, plus local add-ons), mainly on tangible goods and some digital products and services. Since South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018), remote sellers can have nexus through economic thresholds, typically more than USD 100,000 of sales into a state. Taxability of freelance services varies by state. Deloitte 2026 confirms there is no federal VAT or sales tax; states and localities levy sales tax.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: There is no single comprehensive federal privacy law (sectoral federal laws apply; not captured). State laws apply above thresholds. California's CCPA/CPRA covers for-profit businesses doing business in California that meet at least one test: annual gross revenue above USD 26.625 million (inflation-adjusted figure for 2025–2026, counting revenue from all sources); buying, selling or sharing the personal information of 100,000 or more California consumers or households a year; or deriving at least 50% of annual revenue from selling or sharing personal information. Most solo freelancers fall below all three, but other state privacy laws have their own thresholds (not captured).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: The FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule ('30-day Rule') governs online sales of merchandise. You need a reasonable basis for any shipping time you state; with no stated time, you must reasonably expect to ship within 30 days. If you learn you cannot ship on time, you must get the customer's consent to the delay. Without consent, you must promptly refund all money paid for the unshipped goods, without being asked. There is no general federal cooling-off right for online purchases; the FTC Cooling-Off Rule covers door-to-door and off-premises sales (not captured). State laws add further rules.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Qualified business income (QBI) deduction, section 199A: sole proprietors (Schedule C freelancers) may deduct up to 20% of net QBI, limited to 20% of taxable income before the deduction minus net capital gain (IRS Form 8995 instructions). For specified service businesses (SSTBs: consulting, law, health and similar), the deduction phases out above a taxable-income threshold ($197,300–$247,300 for single filers in the 2025 instructions). The One Big Beautiful Bill Act kept the deduction beyond 2025 and, from tax years starting after 31 December 2025, adds a $400 minimum deduction for taxpayers with at least $1,000 of QBI (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
